summary: Continue active Bonk & Bolt stewardship toward the 2030-quality full 3D cartoon open-world RPG vision; this bounded production-rig bridge does not complete the lifetime objective.

The sole write lane remained game-library/014-bonk-and-bolt. Final shared-workspace inspection found active foreign work in slots 012, 013, 015, 016 and 017 with six foreign active shared seams and no overlap; no foreign file or shared registry was edited.

Blender remained unavailable, but a production-source Quaternius Animated Men library was present in the workshop. The selected seam therefore integrated one licensed Human skeletal rig instead of creating another procedural world feature.

Man Casual A is recorded as Quaternius Animated Men Pack, CC0-1.0, 493196 bytes, SHA-256 dad8fa3ca2bc7760892f9ff47f544941179e50acb2aa772cf9f035154a37fc58, with a package-local provenance note and canonical source links.

The runtime stores only assets/characters/quaternius/animated-men/man-casual-a.glb and resolves it from import.meta.url. Three.js r160, GLTFLoader and BufferGeometryUtils are local, so moving the whole package to a future asset drive requires no absolute path rewrite.

The GLB exposes one skinned mesh, 31 joints and 11 clips. Exporter-neutral semantic suffixes bind idle, walk and class-specific attack, special and dodge roles while the existing motion system retains class weapon, cue and timing identity.

Human primitives remain loaded until all asset, bounds, skeleton and required-clip checks pass. A deterministic no-request failure route keeps the original Human visible and playable; Toon identity remains intentionally code-native.
Reduced motion stops the production mixer at a static pose while the established high-contrast action cue remains. The visible preference was live-tested and restored before handoff.

No economy, drops, challenges, story, local co-op, robot roles, progression or separate-game ownership rule changed. The focused QA route clears only its staged origin ledger to remove unrelated museum clutter.
Systems passed 236 checks, hero motion passed 8 of 8, co-op camera passed 10 of 10, hero-rig contract passed 7 of 7, package passed 118 checks and HTTP passed 4 of 4.
At 1280x720 the focused route rendered the licensed Human and directly reported production, human-casual-a, CC0-1.0, 31 bones and idle; a bounded W input reported walk.

Pan Slap directly reported slash and attack:slash while the visible Human entered the authored strike with the class pan and cue; a separated later state returned to idle. No sub-frame cadence was inferred from screenshots.

Reduced-motion attack reported reduced-static with visible cue. Forced fallback reported fallback, procedural, original-code and qa-forced-safe-fallback, visibly retained the primitive Human and accepted Pan Slap without a failed network request.

Focused verifier reported 0 errors and 0 warnings, browser warning/error logs were empty, browser tabs were finalized, capability production-character-quality became READY, workspace ownership remained isolated and port 8814 was clean.

The full objective remains active. Continue one bounded high-value seam; prioritize bespoke grip alignment or a provenance-ready Toon/robot production rig when assets support it, otherwise deepen authored consequences without junk volume or generic reward mail.
